title: Payment service slow responses
executive_summary: INC-003 (SEV2): payment-service latency was elevated from about 18:10Z on 2026-09-08 and payment pods looked healthy on the dashboard. Final status is ROOT_CAUSE_IDENTIFIED. The leading hypothesis (H1, confidence 0.85) is that tail-latency degradation inside auth-service is slowing the payment-service calls that depend on it. auth-service p95 rose from about 45 ms to about 1,188 ms (window mean; max 2,653 ms) and p99 rose from about 90 ms to about 1,982 ms, with onset at 18:07Z (met-auth-service-p95_latency_ms-1740-1835, met-auth-service-p99_latency_ms-1740-1835). Error rate rose from 18:08Z (met-auth-service-error_rate-1740-1835). Payment p95 rose from 18:09Z and payment timeout rate from 18:10Z, from a baseline of 0.1 to a mean of 2.9 (met-payment-service-p95_latency_ms-1750-1830, met-payment-service-timeout_rate-1750-1830). Payment p50, error rate and throughput stayed flat, which fits only a subset of calls hitting the slow auth path. Log evidence corroborates the link: auth-service logged queueing on /v1/token/verify from 18:07:11Z, and payment-service logged slow and timed-out calls to the same endpoint from 18:09:13Z. The critic approved the finding. The trigger of the auth queueing is not established.

critic_review.summary: H1 (auth-service tail-latency degradation propagating to payment-service) is well supported and consistent in time. Metrics show auth p95/p99 onset 18:07Z, before payment p95 (18:09Z) and payment timeouts (18:10Z). Critic log queries add direct corroboration: auth-service logs 'Request queue time high for /v1/token/verify' from 18:07:11Z (up to 9.7 s), and payment-service logs 'Call to auth-service /v1/token/verify took 2320-2700 ms' from 18:09:13Z plus 'Upstream timeout calling auth-service after 3000ms' from 18:10:19Z. The same endpoint is on both sides, so the payment slowdown is tied to the auth path, not a generic payment issue. Payment p50, CPU and error rate stay flat, which fits a subset of calls hitting the slow auth path. No deployments occurred in 17:00-18:30Z. H2 is rejected: postgres aggregates are flat, there is no lock or DB-wait signal in auth logs, and there is a 24-minute gap before auth onset. H3 is rejected: the DEBUG change at 17:35Z shows no latency, CPU or error change in payment until 18:09Z. H4 is superseded by the auth-path evidence, since the timed-out calls are explained.

assessments.reasoning: Consistent timing (auth tail onset 18:07Z precedes payment p95 18:09Z and timeouts 18:10Z). Payment logs show the slow calls are specifically to auth /v1/token/verify (2.3-2.7 s, then 3000 ms timeouts), and auth logs show queue-time spikes on the same endpoint from 18:07:11Z. Direct dependency confirmed by topology. Unexplained: auth timeout_rate did not move, and auth logs show slow JWKS refreshes from identity-provider (120-970 ms) which may be a deeper trigger. That is a limitation, not a reason to withhold approval.

Postgres aggregate p95, connections and CPU are flat. No auth-service log references DB waits or lock contention. The first slow statement at 17:43Z precedes auth onset by 24 minutes with no intervening signal. Auth's slow path is queue time on token verify, not DB latency.

The DEBUG change at 17:35Z has no matching payment latency, CPU or error change until 18:09Z. Payment logs show the delay is caused by auth calls, not logging overhead. Only the change record supports it, so it is temporal correlation alone.

The unknown-cause hypothesis is superseded. Payment's own timeout and slow-call logs name auth-service /v1/token/verify as the blocking call, so the cause is identified. Redis and postgres latency are flat, and no PSP-specific slow-call evidence was found.

corrective_actions: Mitigate the auth-service tail latency now: reduce load or shed requests on the slow path, scale out auth-service replicas, or restart degraded instances if queueing persists (met-auth-service-p95_latency_ms-1740-1835).

Reduce payment-service exposure to slow auth calls: review and tighten the auth call timeout (currently 3000 ms) and enable a fallback or circuit breaker for token verification so that slow auth calls fail fast rather than holding payment threads (met-payment-service-timeout_rate-1750-1830).
Confirm recovery by checking that auth-service p95/p99 and error rate return to baseline and that payment timeout rate drops back toward 0.1.
preventive_actions: Investigate the upstream trigger of auth-service queueing, including identity-provider JWKS refresh latency and whether request volume saturated auth-service. Neither has been checked yet (critic alternative explanations).
Add bulkheads or dedicated connection pools for payment-to-auth calls so that a slow auth tail cannot consume all payment capacity.
Set per-dependency SLOs for auth-service p99 and error rate and review timeout budgets across payment and auth call paths.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on auth-service p95 > 200 ms and p99 > 500 ms sustained for 2 minutes, and on auth-service error rate > 1%.
Alert on payment-service timeout_rate > 0.5% and on payment p95 rising while p50 stays flat, as a signature of dependency tail latency.
Add per-endpoint latency and queue-time metrics for auth-service /v1/token/verify, and track request_rate and identity-provider (JWKS) fetch latency to test the saturation and trigger hypotheses.
Alert on auth-service log lines 'Request queue time high' and payment-service log lines 'Upstream timeout calling auth-service'.
Keep the postgres 'report_rollup()' slow-statement warnings under watch (rejected as the cause, but still noisy).
limitations: The trigger of auth-service queueing (for example, identity-provider JWKS latency) was not established.
Auth-service request_rate was not checked, so volume-driven saturation is not ruled out.
The mechanism that slow auth requests block payment calls is inferred from timing and endpoint match, not from a request-level trace.
Auth timeout_rate metric contradicts H1 and was not fully explained.
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
Investigation terminated because: critic verdict APPROVED
conclusion: The most probable root cause of INC-003 is tail-latency degradation in auth-service, which began around 18:07Z and propagated to payment-service through its token verification calls, producing elevated payment p95/p99 and timeouts while payment median latency and error rate stayed flat.
